source.title: A Neuro-inspired Interpretation of Unlearning in Large Language Models through Sample-level Unlearning Difficulty
source.authors: Xiaohua Feng; Yuyuan Li; Chengye Wang; Jun-Lin Liu; Li Zhang; Chao-Jun Chen

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present; no apparent truncation or garbling prevents review.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses existing unlearning methods as baselines and proposes a method to improve their sampling efficiency. It does not test whether forgotten knowledge can be recovered by the attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments assess sample-level unlearning difficulty and MRD-based sampling, not recovery after unlearning. The paper's ordinary unlearning-completeness and utility tables do not test fine-tuning recovery, activation edits, quantization, or prompt-only recovery; results for the paper's own MRD-enhanced method versus baselines are not cataloged as attack-recovery results.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes an MRD difficulty metric and MRD-weighted sampling to improve existing unlearning methods (GA, GradDiff, PO, NPO) on TOFU, WMDP, WHP and SAFE. It reports only standard forget/utility metrics and its own method versus baselines. It runs no relearning, activation-edit, quantization or prompt-based recovery attack. The WHP 'unseen' completion prompts are held-out paraphrases of the instruction, not an attack on the unlearned knowledge. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that unlearning difficulty varies across samples, that MRD captures it, and that MRD-weighted sampling improves the efficiency and effectiveness of existing unlearning methods. They draw no conclusion about recovery of unlearned knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes MRD-based weighted sampling and applies it to existing unlearning baselines; it does not reproduce a recovery attack or the original unlearning recipes as a robustness test.
record.method_sensitivity: Sample selection affects unlearning performance. The MRD calculation fluctuates with small Monte Carlo sample counts and is described as stabilizing as K reaches 50; the paper reports optimal performance at K = 100. It reports MRD fluctuating around 0.64 as δ increases in the tested range.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning difficulty varies across samples. High-frequency and high-probability samples have lower MRD and are reported as harder to unlearn. Random forget-set choice changes method rankings (GradDiff vs NPO).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample-level difficulty and forget-set selection materially affect measured LLM unlearning performance and method comparisons.

record.problems: The study does not test any of the recovery attacks in the claim. The text provides no uncertainty estimates for the reported results. Some MRD relationships are shown in figures and described qualitatively.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's baseline and MRD-enhanced method comparison tables report ordinary unlearning-completeness and utility metrics, not recovery after unlearning; they are therefore outside the claim versions being cataloged.

untested.parts: Forget accuracy and utility are reported (e.g. WMDP avg ~0.25–0.48, near chance only for SGA/CGA, whose MMLU is ~0.25), but no attack is applied, so the 'simple attacks don't recover it' part is untested.
No activation ablation and no blocking-vs-deletion analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
MRD sampling is not evaluated against recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The recorded parameter sensitivity mentions δ ∈ {1,2,3,4} and K stabilising at 50–100. The text lists σ=1e-5 and K=200 in the setup, an internal inconsistency in the paper. This is irrelevant to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports ordinary unlearning-completeness and utility metrics, but does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning.
No relearning fine-tuning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion is tested.
No prompt-only recovery attack is tested.
No counter-method is evaluated for resistance to the listed recovery attacks.

rows.subject: LLaMA2-7B-chat
rows.operation_detail: Compared MRD values with the number of unlearning updates required across samples.

conditions.value: 10 randomly selected; experiment repeated three times

rows.measure: Relationship between MRD and unlearning update count
rows.value: The text says MRD values capture sample difficulty and align consistently with the required update counts.
rows.note: This is a finding about sample-level unlearning difficulty, not recovery of knowledge.
rows.check: This row validates the paper's own MRD metric (MRD vs update count on TOFU) and is shown only in a figure. It is not a measure of unlearning robustness or recovery, so the 'observed' state does not apply to any claim version.

rows.operation_detail: Compared MRD values with the number of unlearning updates required across samples.

rows.measure: Relationship between MRD and unlearning update count
rows.value: The text says MRD values capture sample difficulty and align consistently with the required update counts.

rows.check: This row validates the paper's own MRD metric on WMDP with Zephyr-7B-beta. It is a method-validation result, not a recovery or robustness result; no version applies.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
